title: fanoutqa: Identify the presidents of the United States who served two terms and their respective political affiliations. (ca085ff48e269f74)

chat_history.content: Identify the presidents of the United States who served two terms and their respective political affiliations.

content.content:
User wants list of US presidents who served two terms and political party affiliation. Should provide list. Possibly up to date as of 2025. Two-term presidents: Washington (no party), Jefferson (Democratic-Republican), Madison (Democratic-Republican), Monroe (Democratic-Republican), Jackson (Democratic), Van Buren? No, one term. Lincoln (Republican) served one term (elected 1860, re-elected 1864, died 1865). Actually Lincoln served two terms but died early in second; still considered two terms. He was Republican. Then Grant (Republican) two terms. Cleveland non-consecutive (two terms but not consecutive), but served two terms but not two-term president; but question says served two terms (could include non-consecutive). Probably include Cleveland (Democratic). Then Wilson (Democratic) two terms. Roosevelt (Republican) two terms. Eisenhower (Republican) two terms. Kennedy? No. Johnson? No. Nixon (Republican) two terms? He was elected twice but resigned early; still two terms? He was elected 1968, re-elected 1972, resigned 1974. Usually considered two-term president. Then Reagan (Republican) two terms. Clinton (Democratic) two terms. Bush Sr (Republican) two terms. Obama (Democratic) two terms. Trump? One term. Biden currently serving first term. Also George Washington no party.

Also include modern: Also maybe include John Adams? No.

List all: Washington (No Party), Jefferson (Democratic-Republican), Madison (Democratic-Republican), Monroe (Democratic-Republican), Jackson (Democratic), Lincoln (Republican), Grant (Republican), Cleveland (Democratic) (though non-consecutive), Wilson (Democratic), Roosevelt (Republican), Eisenhower (Republican), Nixon (Republican), Reagan (Republican), Clinton (Democratic), Bush (Republican), Obama (Democratic), maybe also include: William McKinley? He was assassinated early second term, but served two terms? He was elected 1896, re-elected 1900, died 1901; counts as two terms. So include McKinley (Republican). Also include: Harry S. Truman? He served one elected term after succeeding FDR, then elected 1948; considered one full term? He served more than one term? He served 1945-1953, that's one full term (1949-53) and partial. Not two elected terms. So not.

Also include: Dwight D. Eisenhower, etc.

Also include: Woodrow Wilson (Democratic). Also include: William Howard Taft? No.

Also include: Ulysses S. Grant (Republican). Also include: James Monroe, James Madison.

Also include: Theodore Roosevelt? He succeeded McKinley then elected 1904, so one full term.

Also include: Grover Cleveland counted as two terms but non-consecutive; still served two terms.

Also include: James K. Polk? One term.

Also include: James Monroe, etc.

Also include: Martin Van Buren? One term.

Also include: John Quincy Adams? One term.

Also include: James Buchanan? One term.

Also include: James Monroe.

Also include: James Madison.

Also include: Thomas Jefferson.

Also include: Washington.

Also include: Andrew Jackson.

Also include: Abraham Lincoln.

Also include: Ulysses S. Grant.

Also include: William McKinley.

Also include: Woodrow Wilson.

Also include: Franklin D. Roosevelt? He served four terms. He qualifies as served two terms but also more; maybe include but question likely expects two-term presidents (exactly two). But we could note he served more than two. Might exclude.

Better to list those who were elected to two full terms (or served two terms, including partial). Provide table.

Let's compile list chronologically with party.

List:

1. George Washington – No official party (Independent)
2. Thomas Jefferson – Democratic-Republican
3. James Madison – Democratic-Republican
4. James Monroe – Democratic-Republican
5. Andrew Jackson – Democratic
6. Abraham Lincoln – Republican
7. Ulysses S. Grant – Republican
8. Grover Cleveland – Democratic (non-consecutive)
9. William McKinley – Republican
10. Woodrow Wilson – Democratic
11. Warren G. Harding? No.
12. Calvin Coolidge? One term.
13. Herbert Hoover? One.
14. Franklin D. Roosevelt – Democratic (served more than two)
15. Dwight D. Eisenhower – Republican
16. Richard Nixon – Republican
17. Ronald Reagan – Republican
18. Bill Clinton – Democratic
19. George H. W. Bush – Republican
20. Barack Obama – Democratic

Also include: Thomas Jefferson etc.

Check missing: James K. Polk (one). James Buchanan (one). James Monroe etc.

Also include: John Tyler (none). etc.

Thus answer list.

Probably present as table.

Proceed.

content:
**U.S. Presidents who have served two (full) terms – political affiliation**

| # | President | Years in Office (two‑term span) | Political Party* |
|---|-----------|--------------------------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **George Washington** | 1789 – 1797 | **None / Independent** (no formal party) |
| 2 | **Thomas Jefferson** | 1801 – 1809 | **Democratic‑Republican** |
| 3 | **James Madison** | 1809 – 1817 | **Democratic‑Republican** |
| 4 | **James Monroe** | 1817 – 1825 | **Democratic‑Republican** |
| 5 | **Andrew Jackson** | 1829 – 1837 | **Democratic** |
| 6 | **Abraham Lincoln** | 1861 – 1865 (was assassinated early in his second term) | **Republican** |
| 7 | **Ulysses S. Grant** | 1869 – 1877 | **Republican** |
| 8 | **Grover Cleveland** | 1885 – 1889 & 1893 – 1897 (non‑consecutive) | **Democratic** |
| 9 | **William McKinley** | 1897 – 1901 (assassinated early in his second term) | **Republican** |
|10 | **Woodrow Wilson** | 1913 – 1921 | **Democratic** |
|11 | **Dwight D. Eisenhower** | 1953 – 1961 | **Republican** |
|12 | **Richard Nixon** | 1969 – 1974 (resigned early in his second term) | **Republican** |
|13 | **Ronald Reagan** | 1981 – 1989 | **Republican** |
|14 | **Bill Clinton** | 1993 – 2001 | **Democratic** |
|15 | **George H. W. Bush** | 1989 – 1993 (served one term) – *NOTE*: **He served only one elected term**, so **he is **not** on the two‑term list**.  (Included here for clarity.) |
|16 | **Barack Obama** | 2009 – 2017 | **Democratic** |

\* **Party designation** reflects the party under which the president was elected for each of his two terms.  
- For presidents who died or left office early in their second term (Lincoln, McKinley, Nixon), they are still counted as “two‑term” presidents because they were elected to a second term.  
- **Grover Cleveland** is the only president to serve two terms that were **non‑consecutive**; he is therefore included.  
- **Franklin D. Roosevelt** is omitted because he was elected to four terms (more than two).  

### Quick reference (alphabetical by party)

- **Democratic**: Andrew Jackson, Woodrow Wilson, Bill Clinton, Barack Obama, Grover Cleveland (Democratic)
- **Democratic‑Republican**: Thomas Jefferson, James Madison, James Monroe
- **Republican**: Abraham Lincoln, Ulysses S. Grant, William McKinley, Dwight D. Eisenhower, Richard Nixon, Ronald Reagan
- **Independent/No Party**: George Washington

Feel free to let me know if you’d like additional details (e.g., major accomplishments, electoral vote totals, or a timeline).
